name: Japan
summary: No free movement. Japan has no passive investor, golden or retirement visa. EU, US and other passports can run a business under the Business Manager visa (capital of at least JPY 30 million since 16 October 2025), apply for a six-month digital nomad stay (JPY 10 million income, visa-exempt treaty countries only), or qualify under the points-based Highly Skilled Professional status or a normal work visa. Permanent residence takes 1 to 10 years depending on the route.
naturalisation: Naturalisation generally requires 5 consecutive years of residence in Japan, adult age, good conduct, financial stability, and giving up other nationalities; the Ministry of Justice has discretion. Not verified on an official page in this run.
dual_citizenship_note: Japan expects naturalised citizens to renounce other nationalities; dual nationality is tolerated for those holding it from birth until age 22. Not verified in this run.

routes.name: Business Manager visa (Investor/Business Manager)
routes.summary: Residence status for running or managing a business in Japan; capital requirement rose to JPY 30 million on 16 October 2025.
routes.requirements: From 16 October 2025 (ordinance promulgated 10 October 2025): capital or investment of at least JPY 30 million (previously JPY 5 million); a physical office; at least one full-time employee who is a Japanese national, permanent resident or equivalent; that employee must show Japanese ability; applicant needs 3+ years' management or CxO experience or a relevant master's/doctorate; business plan confirmed by a management specialist. Existing holders have 3 years of transition for renewals. Details from Baker McKenzie and advisers; the ISA notice itself was not opened.
routes.family: Dependent status for spouse and children (not detailed).
routes.tax_note: Japan taxes residents on worldwide income; non-permanent residents (under 5 of the last 10 years) are taxed on foreign income only if remitted.
routes.physical_presence: Run the business in Japan; permanent residence normally needs 10 years (general ISA guideline, not verified here)

sources.title: Japan revises Business Manager visa requirements (Feb 2026)

routes.name: Designated Activities - Digital Nomad (six-month visa)
routes.summary: Six-month non-renewable stay for remote workers earning JPY 10 million a year, from visa-exempt countries with a tax treaty with Japan.
routes.requirements: Remote work for a foreign employer or clients; annual income at least JPY 10 million at application, shown by tax or income certificate; private medical travel insurance with at least JPY 10 million medical cover; nationality of a visa-exempt country that also has a tax treaty with Japan (EU member states, the UK and the US appear to qualify per secondary reports; the official chart was not read). Stay up to 6 months, no extension, no residence card, 6-month wait before re-applying. No employment with Japanese organisations. Spouse and children can accompany.
routes.fees_note: Fee not stated on ISA page.
routes.family: Spouse and children of eligible nationality may accompany under Designated Activities, same 6-month limit.
routes.tax_note: Six months stays under 183 days usually do not create tax residence, but the one-year residence (kyosho) test applies if you keep a home.

routes.name: Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) visa, points-based
routes.summary: Points-based status (70 or 80 points) that grants longer stay, family benefits and permanent residence after 3 or 1 years.
routes.requirements: Points for academic background, career, income, age and bonuses; 70 points for HSP(i), 80 for faster permanent residence. Annual income below JPY 3 million is not accepted even with enough points. Permanent residence after 3 years at 70 points or 1 year at 80 points, per secondary guides; ISA table not opened. From 1 April 2027 guidelines add changes (details unverified). Also J-Skip (very high earners/academics, 1 year to PR) and J-Find (graduates of top universities seeking work).
routes.family: Spouse may work full-time; domestic helpers and parents allowed under conditions (not verified).
routes.physical_presence: Live in Japan; PR application needs continuous residence

routes.name: Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services (employment visas)
routes.summary: Standard employer-sponsored work statuses for degree-holders or experienced professionals.
routes.requirements: Job offer from a Japanese employer in a field matching a degree or 10 years' experience (3 years for international services), pay equal to Japanese workers. Not researched in detail; PR normally after 10 years' residence.
